walkthrough: Goal: after the G3 exit, see a changed choice as the mark moving to it, see the press as the control's own shape, and find the layer mask's entry as something to tap.
Entry: on an empty library (2880 x 1800, landscape) draw a closed triangle with the pen. The right island shows Brush in its ink ring.

Selection shape: tap Selection: the bar reads Freehand (in the ink pill), Rectangle, a faint line, Invert, Deselect. Tap Rectangle: the pill slides right and widens to Rectangle (no fade, no second frame); a new tap mid-slide would turn it back from where it is. Hold a finger on Freehand: the grey wash fills exactly the pill's shape round the word, not the 48-point box around it; lift: the pill slides back to Freehand. Tap Selection to put the tool away: the Brush ring draws in where it is (it was gone while the Selection tool was on; it never slides across islands).

Tools: tap Eraser: the ring slides from Brush over Smudge to Eraser. Tap Brushes: it slides back. Hold a finger on Layers: the wash fills the ring's circle, no wider; lift: the layer panel grows from its button, its ring drawn in place (Layers is not one of the tools).

Blend modes: in the layer options Normal is in the pill (in place as the panel opens, no slide). Tap Overlay: the pill moves diagonally down and right across the grid and narrows to Overlay. Under Clipping Mask the row reads a plus and Add Mask in ink, nothing else on the row.
Add Mask: tap it: the Layer Mask row appears under Layer 1 and the footer shows the mask's hint and commands. Tap Layer 1's row: the layer's options come back with Add Mask grey (the layer has one).
Undo and failure: nothing here changes the drawing but the mask (one undo step, as in S24); a grey Add Mask takes no tap. Reopen: no motion state is kept; marks show in place.
